text: Particle mesh Ewald / PME PME transfers the reciprocal Ewald calculation to a mesh and uses FFTs. Distinguish the original Lagrange-interpolation PME from the later B-spline construction of SPME. Problem and representative equations For a neutral triply periodic Coulomb system, Qₘ is charge assigned to mesh point xₘ using weights Wₘ. The reciprocal operator Ĝₕ includes Ewald screening, mesh conventions and interpolation corrections. This schematic describes only the reciprocal contribution; real-space and self terms remain necessary. Qm=∑iqiWm(ri),ϕh=Fh−1 ⁣[G^h FhQ].Qm​=i∑​qi​Wm​(ri​),ϕh​=Fh−1​[Gh​Fh​Q]. Algorithm Assign charges with local Lagrange polynomials, transform the mesh, apply the reciprocal convolution and transform back. Specify the differentiation and particle-gather rules together. A mesh-interpolated field and the derivative of the discrete energy need not give identical forces. Conditions and pitfalls Separate mesh resolution, interpolation order, Ewald cutoffs and force differentiation in error studies. State FFT normalization, k=0 treatment and units. The usual O(N log N) description assumes an appropriate mesh-growth regime and is not an accuracy guarantee. The linked implementation adopts smooth PME with B-spline analytical energy gradients. It does not implement or validate the original 1993 Lagrange-interpolation PME; the original PME equations, sources and applicability remain distinct from this implemented variant. What to check Use a converged direct Ewald calculation for the identical neutral cell. Vary mesh size, interpolation order and screening; measure RMS/maximum energy and force errors and sensitivity to common translations. A gravity-PM test does not validate PME. The companion varies mesh size, B-spline order and common translation for the same neutral periodic charges, comparing against converged direct Ewald and a separately implemented theta integral. The direct-Ewald comparison shares real-space/self terms, so agreement there alone is not independent validation of the entire energy. Check fixed inputs: separate scoped releases Check each example’s inputs, observables, diagnostic definitions and scope. What a passing check establishes depends on its acceptance criteria and differs from a general mathematical guarantee. Historical inputs, measurements and criteria are preserved. Mesh/order convergence of B-spline smooth PME Computation for a fixed target A small smooth-PME example assigns charge with B-splines and evaluates the Ewald reciprocal contribution by FFT. Finite-mesh aliasing permits nonzero net force for this energy-gradient variant; that diagnostic is reported. No exact momentum conservation, long MD, original PME, optimized P³M or slab validation is claimed.
